thread:
Ana: Quick sync — we need a decision on the "dynamic cushion" approach for Dedicated pools. Customer asks: guaranteed baseline + a small elastic cushion that can be borrowed for short bursts, with automatic repayment window. Do we adopt 1) time-bounded borrow + strict repayment, 2) borrow + billing surcharge, or 3) soft-borrow with fallback routing? Need callouts for SLA, billing, and oncall impact.

Ben: +1 to having a repayment window instead of immediate billing. Ops pain if we bill instantly — customers will escalate. How long were you thinking for repayment? 1h? 24h?

Ana: Thinking 6h as default, tunable per contract. Customers with high tail latency want predictable headroom for short events (5–15m spikes). 6h gives us smoothing for transient load without immediately invoking billing disputes.

Ryan: From runtime side, 6h means we either keep KV cache affinity or risk cold starts when cushion is reclaimed. We should define prewarm triggers if cushion used > X% for > Y minutes to avoid latency spikes on reclaim.

Sasha: Suggest defining two thresholds: soft-borrow (<30% cushion used for <10m) — free; hard-borrow (>30% or >10m) — starts repayment clock + prewarm signal. That keeps noise out.

Maria: For product/contract language: we should offer three tiers: Standard (6h, soft-borrow only), Enterprise (24h, surcharge waived up to N minutes/month), and Pilot (custom). Also need a clear telemetry dashboard item: "cushion-uses by tenant" and "repayment events".

Ben: Oncall concerns: when repayment happens we preempt opportunistic workloads. Need guardrails so we don't cascade evictions across regions. Proposal: repayment is phased — evict from non-latency-critical queues first, and if still needed, route to fallback models/regions.

Ana: Good. We also need an auto-fallback policy when cushion drains during a live canary — automatic model fallback to compatible smaller quantized variant rather than killing requests. Thoughts?

Ryan: We already have model variants flagged as "compat-fallback" — we can wire the routing policy to prefer them when cushion>threshold. Will need tests: a chaos test that simulates cushion reclaim during a canary.

Sasha: For billing — instead of immediate surcharge, what about a cumulative monthly buffer? If a tenant borrows 15m across many events but stays below a monthly cap, no surcharge. Above the cap, apply surcharge and a soft throttle until repayment completes. Simpler for sales.

Maria: Agree. Sales warned that per-minute charges are a blocker. Monthly caps + clear overage rules are easier to explain. Also we should add a waiver path for critical launches.

Ben: Ops runbook additions: 1) alert when tenant cushion borrow >50% for >15m, 2) automated mitigation runbook to ramp noncritical preempt, 3) SLA dashboard + pager only on sustained >1h borrow.

Ana: Decision needed by EOD Monday: pick default policy and which tiers get what. Proposal: default = 6h repayment, soft/hard thresholds as Sasha suggested, monthly free buffer = 60m, surcharge above that. Enterprise: 24h repayment + larger free buffer.

Ryan: I'll prototype the routing hook and add a unit test for canary fallback. ETA EOW.

Sasha: I'll sketch the config surface for Console (toggles for repayment window, buffer minutes, surcharge rates) and mockups for "cushion usage" meter.

Maria: I'll draft the contract language and examples for pricing + waiver clause.

Ben: I'll add the runbook snippets and alert thresholds to eng-oncall.

ops-bot: scheduled: create-epic "dynamic-cushion-policy" assigned to @Ana, @Ryan, @Sasha, @Maria, due 2025-04-04

Ana: Thanks all. If anyone sees a hard no on the monthly-buffer approach, flag here. Otherwise we'll lock in the proposal Monday and start implementation. :thumbsup:
